STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat rectangular/square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall). Food sits on the flat surface.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plate, medium size, roughly 20-25 cm across.
b) Reference: each bagel half is about 11-12 cm across. The plate's long edge spans roughly two bagel-half widths plus a margin, about 2.1 bagel lengths, so the width is about 24 cm.
Reconciled width: about 24 cm (square, area about 576 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Bagel half, left: covers roughly 30% of the plate area, so about 170 cm² footprint. Thickness is about 2 cm (a bagel half is a single layer with a domed crumb). Volume about 35 cm³. Bagel bread is low density, so about 0.3 g/ml gives about 40 g... but a toasted bagel half of this size is closer to 60-70 g, so I use 65 g.
- Bagel half, right: similar size, slightly smaller, about 55 g.
- Cream cheese: a generous smear on the left half (about 25 g) and a mound on the right half (about 20 g), so about 45 g total.
- Cucumber slices: about 5-6 thin rounds, each about 1 cm thick and 5 cm across, roughly 30 g total.

Hidden food: none beyond the bagel halves.

STEP 4 - Total mass is about 65 + 55 + 45 + 30 = 195 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Toasted bagel: about 270 kcal/100 g.
- Cream cheese: about 340 kcal/100 g.
- Cucumber: about 15 kcal/100 g.

Energy: bagel 120 g × 2.7 = 324 kcal (using 120 g for both halves combined, rounded to 65+55); cream cheese 45 g × 3.4 = 153 kcal; cucumber 30 g × 0.15 = 5 kcal. Total is about 480 kcal.
